citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., and Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. arXiv:1606.06031.
creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández (CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam)
description: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) is a dataset of narrative passages for evaluating computational models on word prediction requiring broad discourse context. Each passage consists of a context (average 4.6 sentences) and a target sentence, where the task is to predict the last word of the target sentence. Passages are selected such that human subjects can guess the target word given the full passage but not given only the last sentence, ensuring models must rely on broad discourse understanding rather than local context.
name: LAMBADA
publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 annotations per item in the broad-context condition (steps 1 and 2), plus up to 10 annotations in the sentence-only condition (step 3).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects filtered passages through a three-step crowdsourcing pipeline on CrowdFlower: (1) One subject guessed the target word given the full passage (context + target sentence); if correct, (2) a second subject also guessed from the full passage; if also correct, (3) additional subjects (up to 10) tried to guess the target word from the target sentence only, with 3 guesses allowed per sentence. A passage was included in LAMBADA only if both steps 1 and 2 were passed and no subject succeeded at step 3. Subjects were paid $0.22 per page in steps 1 and 2 (10 passages per page) and $0.15 per page in step 3 (20 sentences per page). The same subject could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a strong bias toward proper nouns as target words (48% of target words), followed by common nouns (37%), with verbs (7.7%), adjectives, and adverbs being rare. Proper nouns are hugely over-represented compared to the input data distribution. Additionally, LAMBADA items contain quoted direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% vs. 61%). The dataset is sourced exclusively from unpublished novels (BookCorpus), which minimizes the usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources but also limits genre diversity. The use of unpublished novels was a deliberate design choice to reduce the potential usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources.
rai:dataCollection: Passages were drawn from the BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), a collection of unpublished novels. The corpus (after duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material) contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions. Candidate passages were first filtered by automated language models (excluding passages where any of four LMs assigned probability ≥0.00175 to the target word), then evaluated by human subjects via the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service in a three-step pipeline: (1) one subject guessed the target word from the full passage; (2) if correct, a second subject also guessed from the full passage; (3) if both correct, additional subjects (up to 10) tried to guess from the target sentence alone — the passage was included only if no subject succeeded at step 3. About 1 in 25 input examples passed all selection steps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data is the BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels. After duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material using a stop word list, the corpus contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Passages were composed of a context (minimum number of complete sentences before the target sentence such that they cumulatively contain at least 50 tokens) plus a target sentence whose last word is the prediction target.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web API
rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation performed in the paper is described as very preliminary and only a proof-of-concept study. The dataset is sourced exclusively from unpublished novels, limiting genre diversity. The strict hit-or-miss approach (requiring exact word match) excludes passages where synonymous or plausible alternative continuations exist. Cost considerations precluded using more subjects at stage 1, which could in principle improve filtering quality. The dataset is skewed toward proper nouns and co-reference phenomena, with fewer examples of event-related phenomena such as script-like sequences of events.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The BookCorpus was preprocessed by removing duplicates and filtering potentially offensive material using a stop word list. Passages were structured with a context of minimum sentences cumulatively containing at least 50 tokens, plus a target sentence. Candidate passages were filtered using four language models (a pre-trained RNN, a standard 4-gram model, an RNN, and a feed-forward model trained on BookCorpus): any passage where the target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of the four models was excluded. Novels were pre-assigned to training or development+testing partitions to prevent data leakage.
rai:dataSocialImpact: LAMBADA is intended to promote research in natural language understanding by providing a challenging benchmark that requires genuine broad-context comprehension. The authors hope it will stimulate the development of novel language models that capture non-local discourse phenomena. A public competition was planned to further encourage community engagement.
rai:dataUseCases: LAMBADA is intended as a challenging benchmark for evaluating computational models of natural language understanding, specifically their ability to track and use information from broad discourse context for word prediction. It is proposed as a test set to encourage development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text. The authors also planned a public competition based on the LAMBADA data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models were used to filter out passages that were too easy for standard language models: (1) a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) (Mikolov et al., 2011), (2) a standard 4-gram language model trained on BookCorpus, (3) an RNN trained on BookCorpus, and (4) a feed-forward language model trained on BookCorpus. Passages where any model assigned probability ≥0.00175 to the target word were excluded.
